A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same AerialVG work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix; the supplementary material mentioned in Sections 5.1 and 5.5 is not included in either supplied file.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1–2, component ablations in Table 3, and a drone-image experiment in Section 5.5 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results, component ablations and drone-image experiment in Tables 1–3 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The GroundingDINO-based architecture, Hierarchical Cross-Attention, Relation-Aware Grounding, score combination, losses and two-stage training procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VisDrone-derived AerialVG dataset, RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg and DJI M30T aerial-image test. Changed dataset citations do not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same comparators: TranVG, Dynamic-MDETR, SimVG and Grounding DINO. No comparator is added, removed or replaced within either experiment.

E3.justification: The zero-shot and fine-tuning settings, Top-1/Top-5 evaluation, RefCOCO evaluation splits, model configurations and training procedure are unchanged. The drone test retains the stated 50-meter altitude and 4000×3000 image resolution.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same baseline, attention-only, relation-only and combined ablations. Section 5.5 and Figure 6 retain the same real-world generalization example, with no additional robustness or error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The same point-estimate reporting practice is retained.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged, including AerialVG's fine-tuned Top-1/Top-5 scores of 50.01/87.00. Dataset statistics and plotted content are unchanged, and Figure 6 retains the same qualitative prediction and score of 0.70.

T1.justification: The attention-update equations and loss definitions in Equations (1)–(4), including their mathematical explanations, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about introducing the AerialVG task and dataset, the two model components, superior aerial-grounding performance and competitive RefCOCO results.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of attention improving candidate retrieval and relational reasoning improving target selection. Section 6 retains the limitation concerning unstructured backgrounds and environmental context.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same backbones, feature scales, token limit, layer counts, loss weights and attention hyperparameters. Annotation instructions and the promised future code release at the same repository address are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3's reference [49], Yu et al., Modeling Context in Referring Expressions, is removed. v4 adds Mao et al., Generation and Comprehension of Unambiguous Object Descriptions, as [30] and changes the RefCOCO/RefCOCO+ citations accordingly. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'Expriment' to 'Experiment' and 'remain their hierarchical structure' to 'retain their hierarchical structure,' with another small introduction wording edit. It also updates author order and affiliations and adds contribution/correspondence footnotes; section organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is slightly reduced in size, the new author footnotes alter the first-page layout, printed page numbers are removed, and references reflow. All six figures and three tables retain their content and basic structure.

improvement.justification: v4 provides small copyediting and author-attribution clarifications alongside a limited citation replacement and layout adjustments. The method explanation, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain essentially identical, supporting no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
